target_customer: Large apparel and general retailers (American Eagle and Old Navy are named customers) that pay for ceiling mounted RFID inventory tracking
problem: Stores lack accurate real-time inventory, causing stock-outs, cancelled online orders and slow checkout lines.
business_model: Hardware plus software subscription installed in stores (RFID sensors, computer vision, analytics)

founders.name: Spencer Hewett
education: Washington University in St. Louis, dropped out for the Thiel Fellowship
founders.background_notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 2022 per a job listing; company describes team experience in satellites, RFID readers and store rollouts. Education and fellowship from a Wellfound profile, a single source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable ceiling mounted RF sensing with item-level accuracy needed custom radio hardware, signal processing and store installation at scale, which is research grade for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary hardware and large chain deployments with installed sensors create strong switching costs, though RFID itself is an established technology.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy of the ceiling sensor wedge was found; an ABI Research note frames Radar as a second generation RFID entrant and incumbents as needing to innovate.

market_need_then: Retail inventory accuracy was a long-standing pain and RFID was being touted by retailers, but 2013 sources on demand for this specific wedge were not found.

branding.domain_note: Uses goradar.com, not radar.com; the exact .com belongs to a different Radar location platform company.

identity.logo: Wordmark logo; no visual description in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Bold, confident and playful: all-caps headlines, short punchy taglines such as GET ON OUR RADAR

rebrands.why: A CB Insights note says RADAR was formerly Automaton; a RADAR trademark was filed in Nov 2016 by Automaton, Inc. and registered in June 2018. The rename date and reason are not sourced.

branding.community_and_virality: Mostly trade press and retail podcasts; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Short evocative name but a very common word shared with other companies, and only trade-press visibility was found.

outcome_analysis: RADAR took a decade to reach scale, building ceiling mounted RFID and computer vision hardware sold to large retailers. It raised a $30M Series A in July 2023 and a $170M Series B at a reported $1B valuation in May 2026, with customers such as American Eagle. Hard hardware, long enterprise rollouts and a deep installed base explain the slow but strong path. Early product details from the 2013 period are not documented in sources found.
notes: Aggregators list a 2019 round of about $16M and total funding anywhere from $63M to $261M; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. The company's early years (2013 to 2018) and the Automaton name are poorly documented; the YC batch year may reflect the original company. A same-named Radar location platform (founded 2016) is unrelated. No dated 2013 competitor sources exist so the list is empty. Customer counts (1,000 to 1,400 stores) are company claims.
